title: TextNGEditor tests must set initial view explicitly, no implicit default
answers: How should I write a test for a specific Text v2 editor view (Write/Preview/Split)?
Why do TextNGEditor tests use a ControlledEditor wrapper with an explicit initialMode/view?
TextNGEditor.test.tsx conventions for selecting view mode
body: Convention: TextNGEditor is a controlled component with no production default of its own - the real default lives only in TextNGPanel.tsx. Tests in editor/TextNGEditor.test.tsx use the `ControlledEditor` wrapper and explicitly select the view they need via the `enterWriteMode`/`enterSplitMode`/`enterPreviewMode` helpers rather than asserting on or relying on an implicit initial view, since the wrapper's own `useState<ViewMode>` default is just a test convenience, not a product behavior.

search: TextNGEditor tests must explicitly set initial view mode using enterWriteMode/enterSplitMode/enterPreviewMode helpers via the ControlledEditor wrapper, never relying on implicit defaults. TextNGEditor is a controlled component with no production default; the true default lives only in TextNGPanel.tsx. The ControlledEditor wrapper's own useState<ViewMode> default is test convenience only, not product behavior, so tests must assert on what they explicitly select, not on wrapper defaults. Convention applies specifically to public/app/plugins/panel/text/v2/editor/TextNGEditor.test.tsx test helpers and test cases.
